label: verify-bm-safety-lca

claims.claim: All 14 Formlabs SLA resin SDS carry H317; Rigid 10K and Silicone 40A H317 alone; Durable V2 and High Temp V2 are H360; Flexible 80A V2 and High Temp V2 are H318; so the two H360 resins should be excluded from a public proof of concept.
claims.source_says: High Temp V2: "H318 Causes serious eye damage H317 May cause an allergic skin reaction H360 May impair fertility. May impair fetus." Durable V2: "H317 ... H360 May damage fertility or the unborn child."
claims.note: I re-read 6 of the sheets (Rigid 10K, Silicone 40A, High Temp V2, Durable V2, Flexible 80A V2) and they match, but I did not check all 14, and the exclusion advice is a judgment.

claims.claim: Formlabs says cleaned parts, cured resin and sintered powder cannot be recycled, and liquid resin and resin-laden solvent may be hazardous waste, so nothing printed may be called recyclable.
claims.source_says: "cannot be recycled. Discard cleaned parts and cured (hardened) resin as household waste." and "Liquid resin (whether pure liquid, dissolved in solvent, or partially cured) may be classified as hazardous waste in your region"
claims.note: Both Formlabs pages say this; the powder page also repeats "cannot be recycled"; the 'may not be called recyclable' step is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Formlabs calls Nylon 11 'bio-based' with no percentage or supplier; the only 100% bio-based carbon (ASTM D6866, castor oil) figure is Arkema's own Rilsan PA11 INVENT NAT sheet and cannot be transferred.
claims.source_says: Formlabs: "legacy strong, highly ductile bio-based material." Arkema: "natural Polyamide 11 powder made from 100% renewable source (castor oil)"; table lists Bio-based carbon content, test ASTM D6866.
claims.note: Formlabs page gives no percentage; I did not confirm the numeric 100 in the scrambled table, but the 100% renewable castor oil statement is there.

claims.claim: EU Directive 2024/825 (applies from 27 September 2026) names 'biobased' and 'biodegradable' as generic environmental claims prohibited unless recognised excellent environmental performance can be shown.
claims.source_says: "'biodegradable', 'biobased' or similar statements that suggest or create the impression of excellent environmental performance. Such generic environmental claims should be prohibited when recognised excellent environmental performance cannot be demonstrated"
claims.note: The wording is in a recital and the text says Member States apply the measures "from 27 September 2026"; the UK-guidance remark was not checked.

overall: Three of four key claims are supported by the original sources; the SDS claim matches on the six sheets I re-read but I did not check all 14.
